full_judgment:
12. The decision reported in 156 Indian cases 912 does not apply to the facts of the present case inasmuch as the question in that decision was whether a certain mosque being used for a long time for worship is a dedicated property. Moreover, it is noticed that in the case before me the dedicated mosque does not stand on the site of the tank. The tank is another property distinguished from the site where the mosque stands. In the case reported in 152 Indian case 50 the question was whether a mosque was a public wakf or not. In the present case the court of appeal below has concurred with the views of the trial Court that the mosque is a public wakf. In that view that decision is of no assistance to the learned Advocate for the petitioners. It has been submitted that an appendix or an annexure of a Wakf property, i.e. the mosque should also be presumed to be a dedicated property and it becomes a Wakf by user. According to the learned Advocate for the plaintiff the tank being annexed to the mosque, it should be presumed that the tank is also a dedicated property. In support of this contention references have been made to the aforesaid decisions reported in 152 I.C. 50 and AIR 1976(SC) 1569. In the case reported in 152 I.C. 50 certain parts of a building were used as a mosque. The parts of a building having been used for a long time as a mosque, the mosque was presumed to have been duly dedicated. The question in that case further was, should this presumption of dedication he extended to other buildings and lands included within the compound wall which might be regarded as appurtenant to the mosque or the tomb. In the case reported in A.I.R. 1976 (S.C) 1569 the question was whether the site of the mosque is a wakf property or whether the adjunct to the mosque which also was used for religious purposes becomes a part of the mosque itself. In that case facts are that the adjunct to the mosque was used for religious purpose. For the purpose of my decision the remaining decisions cited by the learned Advocates need not be discussed. 

 13. In the instant case the mosque which has been held to be public Wakf by both the courts below stands on a site or property distinguished from the property in schedule 1(kha) i.e. the tank. The area of the tank is 1.18 acre. In the absence of any evidence that the entire income of the tank was solely used for the maintenance of the mosque and burning of lights in it, or that the tank was solely used for religious, charitable or pious purposes or that the tank was dedicated to Allah, the ratio-decadent in the aforesaid decisions that the property being an appendix or adjunct to the mosque and used for religious purposes, there is a presumption of dedication of the property in rahelillah, does not apply in the present case.
